newsitem.title: INDIA: India's rulers, Congress try to sidestep polls.
newsitem.headline: India's rulers, Congress try to sidestep polls.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition and its Congress Party foes launched a last-ditch effort on Friday to avoid fresh elections by finding a successor to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, leaders of both sides said.
United Front and Congress officials held informal talks throughout the day in a bid to settle on a leader new without having to go to the polls for the second time in a year.
"We are expecting a change in leadership," Hannan Mollah, a deputy of the Communist Party of India-Marxist, told Reuters after Deve Gowda moved the confidence motion in the lower house.
"There is an awareness that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has to be fought together."
United Front and Congress leaders said talks to find a consensus candidate for the top job would probably follow the parliamentary vote of confidence scheduled for later on Friday.
Deve Gowda faced almost certain defeat, and some parliamentarians said he could step down before the vote.

Bitter foes during the general election campaign last year, the 15-party United Front and Congress joined hands after the polls to put an abrupt end to the right-wing Hindu nationalist BJP's 12-day stint in power.
But Congress president Sitaram Kesri abruptly withdrew support to Deve Gowda on March 30, saying the governing coalition was trying to marginalise India's oldest party.

Congress deputies said a deal was being hammered out to replace Deve Gowda in an attempt to avoid elections, which politicians said could be held by June if the impasse continued and would almost certainly strengthen the BJP.
"Either before the vote or after, a new leader will be chosen," said Jayanthi Natarajan, a Congress deputy. "We believe the United front has already named its candidate."
Shankarsinh Vaghela, chief minister of Gujarat state and a BJP dissident, said: "A new leader will be chosen...We will not have elections."

Speculation centred on G.K. Moopanar, a former Congress member who left the party last year and joined the United Front, and the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh state, Chandrababu Naidu. But Naidu said he was not a candidate.
United Front leaders said they would not abandon Deve Gowda before the vote, but would hold a crucial stock-taking meeting after parliament took its decision.
Asked if the United Front would try to strike a deal with Congress, coalition spokesman Jaipal Reddy said: "That will depend on the meeting in the evening."
Congress leader Ghulam Nabi Azad said it was possible his party would lead a new coalition.
The confidence vote had initially been scheduled for 8 p.m. (1430 GMT), but was expected to be held later in the evening because a long list of deputies wished to speak.

Expectations that the centre-left coalition and Congress would be able to back a joint candidate to replace Deve Gowda pushed up share prices on Friday. The Bombay bourse's key index ended up nearly one percent at 3,633.73 points.
News that lawmakers would hold a special session on April 21-23 to take up the investor-friendly budget, announced in February but still before parliament, also spurred the rally.
The odds were stacked against Deve Gowda as both Congress and the BJP had vowed to vote against him.
His alliance controls 178 votes in the 542-member lower house of parliament. Congress has 140 votes, while the BJP and its four allies control 193.
